data.name: Maithily
data.gender_notes: Maithily is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Maithily is derived from the Sanskrit word 'maithuna', which means union or togetherness. This name signifies the mother of the earth, nourishing and providing for all living beings. The name Maithily carries the meaning “Mother of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maithily usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine and the power of creation and nourishment.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maithily total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

This concept is deeply rooted in Hindu texts and literature, symbolizing the unity and harmony between various aspects of life, such as love, devotion, and nature.

It is a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things in the universe and the importance of maintaining balance and harmony in our lives.

historical_references.reference: Maithily was a prominent Jaina scholar and monk during the Gupta Empire (c. 320-550 CE). He is best known for his work 'Agama-Pravacana-Sastra', a commentary on the Agamas, the Jain canonical texts. 'Agama-Pravacana-Sastra' was instrumental in preserving and interpreting Jaina doctrines for future generations.
historical_references.context: Jaina scholar and monk, author of 'Agama-Pravacana-Sastra'

historical_references.reference: Maithily is also mentioned in the 13th century Jaina text 'Harivamsa-prabandha' as a Jaina saint who lived during the early centuries of the Common Era. The text describes him as a follower of Mahavira and a teacher of the Jaina monk, Vidyanandasuri. He is also credited with writing commentaries on various Jaina scriptures.
